cross_sector_overview: Across every sector, reform is colliding with tighter funding and delivery capacity: the NDIS Thriving Kids rollout and provider closures, higher education cuts and mergers, housing delivery scrutiny, and record-spending credit warnings all point to a fiscal-repair environment. Workforce and provider-market strain (care wages, ECEC retention, migration pipelines) and tightening regulatory obligations (critical infrastructure, NDIS registration) create PEPI demand for transition planning, Commonwealth-state negotiation support, commissioning and evaluation design, and savings and assurance reviews.

synthesis.brief: Aged care waitlist deaths are rising amid a funding backlog for about 100,000 people. Home care package supply and the Support at Home (SaH) rollout remain the main pressure points, with providers saying they have capacity but need funding certainty. Contribution settings are contested: the Coalition and Greens are opposing the private health 'pensioner penalty', and peak bodies are pushing back on the 2.55% AN-ACC increase. Expect more pressure on package release, pricing and care-minute compliance settings, and demand for implementation and evaluation support.

synthesis.brief: Both trusted sources (AFR, Canberra Times) point to fiscal pressure: a global credit agency has warned over record government spending, and the budget is framed as timid yet set to spark a major political fight. Expect tighter scrutiny of spending growth, so agencies should plan for savings, efficiency and prioritisation reviews and for demand for budget-repair and cost-assurance advisory work. State-level signals include NSW coal royalties for budget repair and a Victorian emergency services funding boost.
